name: Answer patient and clinician inquiries
summary: The bilingual contact centre answers calls and web messages from patients and clinicians' offices about results, locations, preparation, requisitions, appointments and reports. Representatives verify who is calling before discussing any patient's tests, look up the requisition in the LIS, explain status, log report copy requests for the reporting team, research missing results with the laboratory and pass complaints to patient relations. Most contacts are settled in a single call of a few minutes; queues build at morning peaks, and contacts that need the laboratory's answer wait hours or days for a callback.

baseline.org_archetype: A large Canadian community laboratory company with a bilingual contact centre of about 110 representatives in Brampton, London, Laval and Winnipeg.
baseline.notes: COVID-19 testing in 2020-2022 raised call volumes sharply and is not modelled. Critical result calls, insurance, workplace and billing lines are separate processes.

trigger: A patient, clinician's office or portal user calls the customer care line or sends a web form or email.
end_state: The inquiry is answered, a report request or complaint is passed on, the caller is transferred to the right team, or the caller hangs up.

volume.seasonality: Peaks on weekday mornings when centres open and clinics call, on Mondays and after holidays; COVID-19 testing in 2020-2022 caused large surges.

evidence.note: Volume from the organisation file's process map; the channel and topic mix is the author's estimate.

Duties from the company's customer care postings; FTE on inbound inquiries is the author's estimate; the rest of the 110 representatives do order entry, outbound campaigns, result calls and special accounts.
Escalation of contentious items is described; FTE covering escalations and call quality scoring is an estimate.
Intraday queue management and complaint oversight spread across inquiries; estimate.

roles.title: Charge technologist
roles.department: Community laboratory testing (The model laboratory Laboratories)

evidence.note: Representatives work with the laboratory on testing processes and results; the charge technologist answering their queries is an assumption.

systems.name: Contact centre telephony with IVR, queues and call recording
CRM for client accounts, sales pipeline and service cases
Laboratory information system (orders, accessioning, results, autoverification rules)
eResults provider portal and EMR results delivery
The consumer health service patient portal and online test shop
Online appointment booking and centre queue management
Public website test directory and location finder

steps.name: Route the call through the IVR or receive the web message
steps.description: The caller dials the toll-free line, chooses English or French and patient or clinician in the IVR and hears recorded messages about hours and the online location finder; web form messages and emails land in a shared message queue instead.

error.defect_description: Caller picks the wrong menu option and reaches the wrong queue.

next.condition: answered by the IVR message or hangs up

evidence.note: One toll-free line for patients and providers with online forms by subject (ci_contact); channel shares are estimates.

steps.name: Caller waits in the queue
steps.description: The call waits for the next free representative in its language queue; at morning peaks, when centres open and clinics start calling, the wait grows and the IVR offers a callback instead of holding.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Mean speed to answer of 75 seconds in US centres (babel21); the morning peak, callback and abandonment shares are estimates.

steps.name: Telephony system calls the customer back
steps.description: When a representative becomes free the telephony system dials the customer who chose a callback and connects the call, keeping the customer's place in the queue.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Queue callback was a common contact centre feature by 2019; timing is an estimate.

steps.name: Answer the call and identify the caller and the reason
steps.description: The representative greets the caller in English or French, asks whether they are a patient, a clinician's office or another client, opens a contact record in the CRM and works out what the caller needs.

error.defect_description: Reason misunderstood, so the caller gets the wrong answer or transfer.

next.condition: about a patient's tests or reports
billing, insurance, workplace or genetics question

evidence.note: Answering inquiries and recording customer information for every contact are listed duties; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Verify the patient's identity or the clinic's authority
steps.description: Before discussing a patient's tests the representative confirms the patient's name, date of birth, health card number and address against the LIS, or for a clinic confirms the clinician and office are the ordering or copy-to provider on the requisition.

error.defect_description: Information disclosed to someone who is not the patient or an authorised provider.

control.basis: Ontario Personal Health Information Protection Act, 2004, Quebec Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector and Manitoba Personal Health Information Act: verify identity and authority before disclosing personal health information

next.condition: clinic asks for a report copy

evidence.note: Disclosure only with consent or as permitted by law (dyn_privacy); the legal rule is named from general knowledge and the shares are estimates.

steps.name: Look up the order and result status in the LIS
steps.description: The representative finds the requisition in the LIS, checks which tests are complete or pending and where the report went, and explains that results go to the ordering clinician, when pending tests are expected and that many results also appear in the patient portal.

error.defect_description: Pending test reported as complete or the wrong requisition read.

next.condition: patient asks for a copy of the result
report must be re-sent to the clinician

evidence.note: Results typically take a day and some are available only from the provider (dplus_faq); the FAQ directs patients to the ordering provider (ci_contact). Times and shares are estimates.

steps.name: Release a result copy to the patient under provincial policy
steps.description: The representative checks the release rules for each test (pathology, genetic and regulated tests go only through the clinician), then emails an encrypted copy or mails it, or guides the patient to register for the portal.

error.defect_description: A restricted result released to the patient.

control.basis: Ontario Personal Health Information Protection Act, 2004, Quebec Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector and Manitoba Personal Health Information Act: verify identity and authority before disclosing personal health information; company result release rules by province

evidence.note: Releasing patient results in line with provincial policies is a listed duty (ccr_brampton); restricted test types (dplus_faq); encrypted email (dyn_privacy).

steps.name: Give location, hours, preparation, requisition or price information
steps.description: The representative answers from the website location finder, the test directory and preparation sheets: nearest centre and hours, fasting or urine collection instructions, how to fill in a requisition and the price of uninsured tests.

error.defect_description: Wrong preparation instruction, so the patient arrives unprepared.

next.condition: wants an appointment booked or changed

evidence.note: Helping with requisitions, collection, patient instructions and cost questions are listed duties; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Book or change a collection centre appointment
steps.description: The representative opens the online booking system, finds a time at the patient's chosen centre, books or moves the appointment in the patient's name and confirms the email or text reminder.

error.defect_description: Appointment booked at the wrong centre or time.

evidence.note: Booking help by phone is the author's estimate; the booking system is in the organisation file.

steps.name: Log a report copy or re-send request
steps.description: For a clinic that did not receive a report, or a new copy-to provider, the representative confirms the clinic's fax number or EMR delivery, enters the re-send request in the LIS for the reporting team and records the contact.

error.defect_description: Wrong fax number entered, so the copy is misdirected.

evidence.note: Acting on phone and fax requests from physician offices is a listed duty; the copy request volume is set to agree with the result reporting workflow.

steps.name: Research the problem in the LIS and specimen records
steps.description: For a missing result, an untested specimen, a rejected sample, an add-on test or a lost requisition, the representative checks specimen tracking, comments and the requisition image, and either answers on the call or sends a query to the laboratory or collection centre.

error.defect_description: Cause misread, so the customer gets a wrong explanation.

next.condition: caller upset or issue contentious, escalate

evidence.note: Liaising with other departments and coordinating on turnaround are listed duties; times and shares are estimates.

steps.name: Laboratory answers the representative's query
steps.description: A charge technologist or the bench supervisor reads the query, checks the specimen's status, rejection reason or add-on feasibility in the LIS and on the bench, and replies to customer care.

error.defect_description: Answer based on the wrong specimen.

evidence.note: Representatives work with the laboratory on testing processes and results; role and times are estimates.

steps.name: Call or email the customer back with the answer
steps.description: The representative phones the patient or clinic (or emails when they asked for it), explains what happened and what to do next, such as a recollection, a new requisition or the expected report date.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Contacting customers to collect or give information is a listed duty; timing is an estimate.

steps.name: Transfer the caller to billing, insurance, workplace or genetics
steps.description: For questions handled by another team the representative explains the transfer, warm-transfers or gives the right number (billing line, insurance, corporate clients or genetics) and notes the reason in the CRM.

error.defect_description: Transferred to the wrong team.

evidence.note: Separate lines for billing, corporate clients, insurance and genetics (ci_contact); redirecting customers is a listed duty.

steps.name: Team lead handles an escalated contact
steps.description: The team lead takes over a contentious or upset caller, reviews the record and the laboratory's answer, offers a resolution within policy such as a recollection or a manager callback, and decides whether it is a formal complaint.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Contentious items are escalated to the Customer Service Manager; times and shares are estimates.

steps.name: Log the complaint and pass it to patient relations
steps.description: The representative or team lead records the complaint in the CRM with the patient's details, the centre or test involved and what the patient wants, and assigns it to patient relations for investigation and a written response.

error.defect_description: Complaint logged without enough detail to investigate.

control.basis: ISO 15189 and Accreditation Canada Diagnostics requirements to record and resolve complaints

evidence.note: Owning complaints to resolution is a listed duty (ccr_brampton); privacy complaints go to the privacy officer (dyn_privacy). Accreditation basis named from general knowledge.

steps.name: Read and classify the web message or email
steps.description: During staffed hours a representative opens the next message in the shared queue, reads the subject chosen on the form, checks the sender against the LIS where a patient is named and decides how to answer.

error.defect_description: Message misclassified and answered by the wrong team.

next.condition: clinic asks for a report copy

evidence.note: Online forms by subject (ci_contact) and email, chat and fax responses (ccr_brampton); shares and queue time are estimates.

steps.name: Reply to the message
steps.description: The representative writes a reply from approved templates, adding the location, preparation or status details, and asks the patient to call or use the portal when the answer would disclose health information by unsecured email.

error.defect_description: Reply contains a wrong instruction.

evidence.note: Website messages are not secure and confidential email is encrypted (dyn_privacy); times are estimates.

steps.name: Record the outcome and wrap up the contact
steps.description: After the call or reply the representative selects the reason and outcome codes in the CRM, adds a short note so a repeat caller can be helped quickly and becomes available for the next call.

error.defect_description: Wrong reason code, which distorts the call reports.

evidence.note: Recording every contact and keeping the call log are listed duties (ccr_brampton); post-call wrap-up is 9.4 per cent of agent time in US centres (babel21).

steps.name: Team lead scores a recorded call for quality
steps.description: The team lead listens to the recorded call, scores greeting, identity verification, accuracy and courtesy on the quality form, and gives the representative feedback in the next coaching session.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Contact centre quality monitoring program: a sample of calls per representative scored each month

evidence.note: Call recording is in the organisation file; sample rate of about five calls per representative a month is an estimate.

exceptions.name: Abandoned call
exceptions.description: The caller hangs up while waiting, mostly at the morning peak, and often calls again later.

exceptions.name: Missing or delayed result
exceptions.description: The representative cannot answer from the LIS and must query the laboratory or centre and call back.

exceptions.name: Identity not verified
exceptions.description: The caller cannot confirm the patient's details or is not an authorised provider, so nothing is disclosed.

exceptions.name: Escalation and complaint
exceptions.description: An upset caller goes to the team lead, and some contacts become formal complaints for patient relations.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the call or message to the end of the contact
benchmarks.population: Derived from US contact centre benchmarks

evidence.note: p50 of about 8 minutes is the mean speed to answer (75 seconds) plus a service call of a little over six minutes (babel21); p90 of about one day is the author's estimate, set by web messages answered within a business day and by callbacks after a laboratory query.

benchmarks.unit: share of contacts resolved without a repeat contact
minutes, mean (stated as over six minutes)

evidence.note: The summary states a mean service call of over six minutes; 6.5 is used.

pain_points.description: Morning peaks, when centres open and clinics start calling, lengthen queues and abandonment, and abandoned callers ring again.

evidence.note: The organisation file says morning peaks drive wait times; abandonment and callback shares are estimates.

pain_points.description: Representatives cannot see the bench, so missing results, rejected specimens and add-on requests need a query to the laboratory and a callback hours or days later.
Every patient-specific question needs identity checks, and many patients asking for results are told to contact their clinician because results go to the ordering provider.
About three in ten contacts are repeats because the first contact did not settle the issue, adding volume the queue must absorb.

evidence.note: Industry average FCR 71 per cent.

sources.title: Contact us
sources.supports: One toll-free line (800.565.5721) for patients and for healthcare providers and hospitals, separate lines for corporate clients, insurance, genetics (the model laboratory's genetics service) and billing (800.668.2714); online forms with subjects such as general question, payment question, scientific or clinical question, technical support and set-up; the FAQ tells patients to contact the ordering provider for results.

sources.title: Customer Care Representative, Brampton (job posting #2026-12231)
sources.supports: Shifts Monday to Sunday between 7:00 am and midnight; CAD 19.50 to 22.00 an hour; answers inquiries about services and redirects customers; helps clinicians and patients complete requisitions; supports sample collection, patient instructions and cost questions; owns complaints to resolution; responds by email, phone, live chat, fax, mail and social media; releases patient results in line with provincial policies; records customer information for every contact; acts on phone and fax requests from physician offices; maintains the call log and reports metrics; coordinates with other departments on test turnaround.

sources.title: Bilingual Customer Care Representative (ENG/FRE), London (job posting #2026-12359)
sources.supports: French and English required; CAD 21.00 to 26.50 an hour; handles customer calls and correspondence using several databases; liaises with other departments; identifies, documents and resolves problems and complaints; escalates contentious items to the Customer Service Manager and laboratory; works with the laboratory on testing processes and results; tracks and reports KPIs; Cisco call centre platform listed.

sources.title: The consumer health service frequently asked questions
sources.supports: Reports appear in the portal within 3 hours of the order being entered; results generally take 1 calendar day; genetic, cardiology, pathology and regulated results are available only through the healthcare provider; patients with an overdue report submit a request through Contact Us; customer care line 855.748.1115.

sources.title: Privacy policy
sources.supports: Personal information is disclosed only with consent or as permitted by law; some results are available only from the ordering physician; staff try to confirm preferences for phone messages and do not identify the company in a message unless reporting a critical result; confidential email is encrypted; access and complaint requests go to the privacy officer.

sources.title: First call resolution operating philosophy
sources.supports: Call centre industry benchmark first call resolution 71 per cent, so 29 per cent of customers call back about the same inquiry; each 1 per cent FCR improvement raises satisfaction 1 per cent and cuts operating cost 1 per cent.

sources.title: First call resolution
sources.supports: FCR is measured by agent logging, repeat-call counts within 1 to 30 days or post-call surveys; about 70 per cent industry average by survey; internal no-repeat methods overstate FCR by 10 to 20 per cent.

sources.title: The US Contact Center HR and Operational Benchmarking Report 2021 (summary)
sources.supports: 214 US contact centres interviewed in Q4 2020: mean average speed to answer 75 seconds; mean service call over six minutes; agent time 58.6 per cent talk, 9.4 per cent post-call wrap-up, 11.7 per cent email and web chat, 8.8 per cent idle; mean cost per inbound call USD 7.46. Read from a text copy saved under scratch by earlier work.

assumptions: Repeat contacts about the same issue are counted as separate inquiries in the organisation file's volume, so the step graph does not loop them back; the industry first call resolution of about 71 per cent implies roughly 29 per cent of inquiries are repeats.
Channel mix (85 per cent phone, 12 per cent web forms and email, 3 per cent ended in the IVR) and topic shares are the author's estimates.
Report copy requests are set at about 12 per cent of inquiries so that they match the result reporting workflow, which takes 2 per cent of its 690,000 monthly cases from this process.
Complaints passed on are about 0.35 per cent of inquiries (about 400 a month), within the organisation file's 600 complaints a month from all channels.
Result copies released to patients and booked appointments go to the patient directly; the organisation file lists no business object for them, so they are not in interfaces.produces.

Hands-on times are for an experienced representative; the mean is a little over six minutes per inquiry including those that end before reaching a representative. At 120,000 inquiries a month this implies about 88 FTE of representative time against the 92 FTE stated; the rest of the 110 representatives do order entry, outbound campaigns, social media and special accounts.
The charge technologist role answering laboratory queries and the US contact centre benchmarks are assumptions or proxies; no Canadian laboratory contact centre benchmark was opened.
Web search capacity ran out before this workflow, so sources were limited to pages fetched by address and text copies saved earlier.
Loaded costs are from the organisation file (hourly wage times 1.35).
